summary: Rate-tier synchronization gap causing early 429s for rolling ingest pool
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports persistent 429 responses originating from their dedicated ingest pool during a rolling bulk ingest job. Throttles begin well before expected refill boundaries, causing partial failures and retries in their orchestrator.

Impact:
- 20-30% of ingestion worker tasks receive 429s during a 2h rolling import window.
- Jobs retry and extend total import time by ~3x.
- Customer-facing syncs downstream are delayed; revenue-impacting for nightly ETL.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (customer-managed pool), pool id: dsp-7e1a
- Region: prod-us-west (single AZ failover configured)
- Ingest orchestrator: DataStreamX uploader v2.3 (uses short-lived ephemeral keys per worker)
- Rate config: split-burst pool enabled with priority lanes; route affinity on

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start rolling bulk ingest across 50 workers with ephemeral key fanout
2) Warmup phase runs parallel preflight requests to pin model variants
3) After ~6 minutes into the job, intermittent 429s appear across many workers, intensifying as the job proceeds and more ephemeral keys are minted

Expected behavior:
- Throttling should respect burst credits and sustained refill windows; early 429s should not occur during initial warmup if within burst allocations.

Actual behavior:
- 429s observed consistently before refill boundary; console shows burst credit balance dropping faster than tokens consumed at origin.

Collected artifacts (attached by customer):
- Ingest job logs (timestamps, worker ids), HTTP response headers from throttled requests, ephemeral key creation timeline
- Console screenshot showing per-route and pool-level token balance at time of incident
comments: 2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged receipt. Asked customer for request/response headers and list of ephemeral key timestamps. Escalated to SRE for early triage.

2026-03-12 11:18 - SRE (Mark): Noted odd drift between edge token windows and origin refill. Requested edge proxy logs (edge-proxy-usw-3) and rate-limiter debug metrics for epoch window overlapping at 10:57-11:05.

2026-03-12 13:42 - Customer (Elena, DataStreamX): Uploaded logs and a short trace of worker key creation; called out that workers create ephemeral keys approximately every 30s during the first 10 minutes.

2026-03-12 16:01 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed we have artifacts; running local replay against a staging rate-limiter to attempt reproduction. Noted link to runbook and will update when SRE has metrics.

2026-03-13 09:22 - SRE (Mark): Reproduce attempt on staging using similar ephemeral-key cadence reproduced early 429 pattern. Hypothesis posted to ticket. Planning controlled config change in staging to validate fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: A synchronization gap exists between edge-level token accounting and origin refill epochs when ephemeral keys are created rapidly and route affinity shifts mid-window. Edge proxies appear to attribute token consumption to ephemeral key buckets before central refill has reconciled, causing perceived early exhaustion.

Observed: In staging replay, edge-proxy counters incremented ahead of origin by 2-4s during high fanout; refill window boundaries at origin align to minute epoch while edge had slight drift due to NTP jitter and proxy batching behavior.

Metric evidence: rate-limiter.checkout_latencies and token_delta metrics show spikes at worker-fanout events; per-route burst_credit_balance at edge drops while origin reports pending refill. Related dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl/edge-refill-drift?orgId=1&from=now-30m

Triage action: opened PR to add conservative debounce on edge-side accounting and to tag ephemeral keys with ingestion-session id so origin accounting can coalesce counts before rejecting. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ratelimiter/pull/879
Risk assessment: Low-to-medium risk to change; affects only dedicated pools with short-lived-credential fanout and split-burst enabled. Requires canary rollout in prod-us-west to validate.
Coordination note: Need customer to enable short canary run window; suggested to run gradually with 10% worker concurrency for first validation.
resolution_notes: Workaround (short-term): Instructed DataStreamX to increase ephemeral key TTL to reduce churn (from 30s -> 300s) and to apply client-side jitter on key creation to avoid synchronized fanout. This immediately reduced 429 occurrence in their next test window.

Mitigation (mid-term): Deployed staging fix that adds a 200ms edge-level debounce and tags ephemeral sessions to batch accounting. Staging replay shows 85% reduction in early 429s. PR referenced above contains tests and metrics links.
Planned rollout: Canary rollout scheduled for prod-us-west with 10% of dedicated pool traffic on 2026-03-16, monitored by SRE and on-call. Full rollout contingent on 48h canary results.

Follow-ups: 1) Add diagnostic console panel to show edge-origin token drift per-pool. 2) Update docs with recommended ephemeral key TTL and jitter guidance for dedicated pools. 3) Create a small runbook for customers running high-fanout rolling ingests.
Status: Pending canary. Customer notified of workaround and will validate TTL change in nightly import.
